correctness.rationale: A noncoherent strict orientation is acyclic, so all sinks are forced and recursively deleting them and their in-neighbors gives its unique kernel. A reciprocal edge permits a noncoherent strict suborientation, and restoring those arcs neither introduces adjacency in a kernel nor destroys outgoing absorption. The remaining coherent one-way cycles enforce alternating membership, giving the parity exception and exact probability. For each candidate maximal independent set the selected-vertex gaps are 2 or 3, including the one-gap triangle. Gap constraints involve disjoint sets of edges, with success probabilities u=1-(1-a)² and v=a². Counting marked cyclic selections and dividing by the number of marks gives the weighted sum; its generating series is the logarithmic derivative of (1-uz²-vz³)⁻¹, which gives the root powers with multiplicities. The companion matrix is irreducible and has periods 2 and 3 among its closed walks; the Perron root is simple and dominant. At r=0 the roots are 1,-1/2,-1/2 and implicit differentiation gives 4/9, with the two smaller root powers uniformly negligible when nr stays bounded. For the eight-edge gadget the two sinks are forced, vertices 1 and 5 excluded, and the path 2,3,4 has the two independently switchable internal configurations {3} and {2,4}. Its boundary is unchanged by the switch. The tested blocks use disjoint edges and one success guarantees existence. The binomial lower tail with m≥n/18 proves both stated constants; r=1 follows separately from the Perrin endpoint.
residual_risks: The exact finite enumeration is supplemental; the binomial gadget and spectral arguments give the unbounded-n assertions. The 1/n crossover is an expectation result, not a law of K_n.

originality.rationale: The supported distinction is the edge-weighted partial-reciprocity expectation with its small-r crossover and the typical exponential multiplicity mechanism in the same random-ring model. The equilibrium correspondence, sink recursion, preservation of kernels by reciprocation and endpoint Perrin enumeration are prior mathematics. The exact nonexistence formula is a short consequence of those structural principles on a ring, not sufficient novelty on its own.
residual_risks: No full-text examination of De La Vega or Richardson was possible in this review; unindexed weighted-Perrin or random-kernel results could contain closer precedents.

value.rationale: The ring isolates a substantive effect of reciprocal public-good links. Almost all strictly one-way rings have exactly one specialized equilibrium, whereas any fixed positive edge reciprocity gives exponentially many with high probability, not just an expectation inflated by rare instances. The exact mean identifies a separate, motivated rare-reciprocity scale and allows finite-size comparison; the forced-sink gadget explains how local choices accumulate in the typical case.
residual_risks: Neither an exact typical growth rate nor a distributional law in the 1/n window is supplied.
